title: plugin-approvals: a `field` or `position` approver step has no "not the submitter" guard, so a manager who submits their own request can approve it
body:
Ruled: 6377888641 · batch #9 item 1 (#25496, 6377842908) · letter B · 2026-10-24T00:43:45Z (step option `excludeSubmitter`, default off; empty set escalates per ADR-0042 or reroutes to the fallback)

Filed from the objectstack-ai/hotsrm v0.1 platform evaluation, 2026-10-23, spec 18.0.0.

## What was measured
- A two-level admission approval: step 1 approver `field` (the category manager on the record), step 2 `position` (procurement director). Both resolve and work.
- When the category manager submits the admission themselves, step 1 resolves to the same person and they approve their own submission. Nothing in the step declaration excludes the submitter.
- Every procurement control framework (SOX-style segregation of duties, Chinese SOE procurement rules T/CFLP 0016) treats self-approval as a finding, so an app has to add it by hand: an `expression` approver, or a validation rule blocking "submitter == approver" before entry. Both are easy to forget and are per-flow.

## Wanted
- A step-level option (`excludeSubmitter: true`, or a flow-level default) that removes the submitter from the resolved approver set and, when the set becomes empty, escalates per ADR-0042 or reroutes to the step's fallback, instead of silently letting the request through.
- The approval record should show when the exclusion changed the route.

## Acceptance
With the option on, a request whose resolved approver is its submitter is routed to the fallback or escalated, never approved by the submitter; with the option off, behaviour is unchanged.

Dedupe words: approvals self-approval submitter excluded approver segregation of duties excludeSubmitter fallback.
